text:
maria_g: heads up — hit a dup-credit case during a partition handoff. consumer repo restarted mid-handshake and we ended up emitting credits twice for ~2k events. attaching short log excerpt.

jonathan: ugh. can you paste the repro steps? is this the same late-arrival sequence we've seen before or something new?

maria_g: steps: 1) produce events to partition p3 2) trigger planned handoff (scale down) 3) broker moves ownership, consumer B picks up 4) consumer B crashes after applying local cache but before writing safepoint -> on restart both A and B think they own range -> duplicates. logs: 
```
2026-02-11T12:03:10Z INFO commit.safepoint pending write
2026-02-11T12:03:11Z ERROR consumer.crash signal SIGTERM
2026-02-11T12:03:12Z INFO consumer.start replaying from offset 42
2026-02-11T12:03:13Z INFO credits.emit 42..128 produced
```

neil_r: so root cause is non-atomic transition: ownership update vs safepoint persistence. we need a canonical owner marker in storage that is only flipped when safepoint persisted.

sophia: two obvious patterns: (A) master-backed safepoint commit: coordinator writes safepoint+owner in a single txn and only then we consider the handoff complete, or (B) idempotent sinks with idempotency keys derived from (partition, epoch, offset-range). both have tradeoffs.

lisa_ops: (A) means cross-region coord and stronger lease semantics. might increase tail latency for handoffs. (B) pushes complexity into downstream accounting and requires us to carry epoch metadata on every emitted credit. storage + index cost increases.

jonathan: quick thought: can we create a lightweight "safepoint manifest" object per partition with fields (version, last_applied_offset, owner_id) and use CAS on manifest write? producer/consumer do a CAS to claim owner after verifying last_applied_offset hasn't regressed.

maria_g: CAS manifest sounds attractive. If manifest write fails, consumer should abort handoff and backoff. helps avoid split-brain. need to handle tombstones when partition is deleted.

neil_r: also consider a fast-path where small handoffs (no credits in-flight) are purely in-memory + last-ack check, i.e., optimize common case. for larger state we fall back to manifest CAS.

sophia: implementation notes: add manifest to compacted kv-table keyed by partition-id. manifest value must be small and include a monotonic handoff-epoch. we'll bump epoch on every attempted handoff. credits emitted attach epoch. reconciliation pass periodically verifies (epoch in events) matches manifest and drops/marks dup emissions.

lisa_ops: ops/cost note: that reconciliation pass will need to scan recent events; suggest we bound retention to N minutes and only reconcile if we detect a handoff mismatch. avoids full reprocessing.

jonathan: edgecases: what about network partition where both sides CAS concurrently and one wins but the loser still emits before it sees loss? CAS will let loser know on next manifest read but we must ensure idempotency keys prevent double-write to the billing sink. so hybrid: CAS+idempotent-sink for defense in depth.

maria_g: action items: 1) spike CAS-manifest prototype (neil + maria) 2) design idempotency header for credits (sophia) 3) add reconciliation guardrails and retention bounds (lisa_ops). I'll open PRs and a short RFC doc.

deploy-bot: scheduled a canary for spike branch on staging at 2026-02-12T02:00Z :rocket:

jonathan: sounds good. small ask: include a datapoint perf estimate for CAS roundtrip (p99). if it's >50ms we may need async handoff confirmation UI in console.

maria_g: will measure and include in the RFC. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
